builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Skill Adapter: Personalized Modification and Online Routing of General-Purpose Skills
summary: The method replaces static general-purpose skill libraries with per-user Adapters that encode local adjustments, plus a routing agent that maintains an online task-level skill library and preloads candidates for later subtasks. The cost is an additional RL training loop for two decision policies, an adapter storage and routing layer, and runtime overhead for candidate preloading and applicability rechecking. It can fail when user-specific adjustments are sparse or noisy, when the routing agent mis-selects under expanding pools, and when the RL optimization overfits to benchmark feedback signals rather than production execution traces.
rationale: The approach targets agent skill management rather than inference efficiency, and its RL-based training plus online routing infrastructure exceeds what a small team on constrained infrastructure can deploy and validate without dedicated effort.
technique: Skill Adapter: personalized skill adapters and online routing

claims.statement: The method replaces static general-purpose skill libraries with per-user Adapters that encode local adjustments, plus a routing agent that maintains an online task-level skill library and preloads candidates for later subtasks. The cost is an additional RL training loop for two decision policies, an adapter storage and routing layer, and runtime overhead for candidate preloading and applicability rechecking. It can fail when user-specific adjustments are sparse or noisy, when the routing agent mis-selects under expanding pools, and when the RL optimization overfits to benchmark feedback signals rather than production execution traces.
Improves task success rates by an average of 11.43 percentage points over SkillRL on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SkillsBench, with reduced mean execution time; advantage holds at 1,000-skill pools.
